titleEn: Whole House Renovation on the North Shore: North Vancouver vs West Vancouver Costs in 2026
titleZh: 北溫與西溫整屋裝修2026：造價、工期與項目完整指南
excerptEn: A single-family home renovation on the North Shore costs $180–$500/sq ft depending on scope. Reno Stars breaks down what each neighbourhood actually costs, based on 58 real projects across Metro Vancouver.
excerptZh: 北溫和西溫的獨立屋裝修造價為每平方呎180至500加元，視乎工程範圍而定。聚星裝修根據大溫哥華58個真實項目，逐一分析各區實際造價。
contentEn:
On the North Shore, a whole-house renovation is not a cosmetic upgrade — it is a structural, financial, and logistical undertaking that requires navigating steep slopes, older building stock, and some of the highest construction costs in Metro Vancouver. In 2026, a full renovation on a single-family home in North Vancouver or West Vancouver starts at approximately $180 per square foot and can exceed $500 per square foot for premium remodels with structural changes, heritage preservation, or challenging site conditions.

Reno Stars has completed projects in both municipalities. This guide covers what each neighbourhood actually costs, which permits are required, and how long each scope typically takes.

What Does a Whole House Renovation Cost on the North Shore in 2026?

The short answer is that it depends on three factors: the scope of work, the condition of the existing structure, and whether the property requires seismic upgrading, slope engineering, or heritage review. Based on 58 projects across Metro Vancouver, Reno Stars' data shows the following cost ranges for whole-house renovations on the North Shore:

  • Cosmetic renovation (flooring, paint, cabinet refinishing, bathroom refresh): $80,000–$180,000 for a 2,000 sq ft home
  • Standard full renovation (kitchen and bathrooms rebuilt, flooring, electrical, plumbing, drywall): $180,000–$380,000 for a 2,000 sq ft home
  • Premium whole-house remodel (structural changes, custom millwork, high-end finishes, engineering required): $380,000–$800,000+ for a 2,000 sq ft home

West Vancouver homes tend to skew toward the premium range. Many West Van properties were built in the 1960s and 1970s with post-and-beam construction that requires structural engineering review before any demolition. North Vancouver homes more commonly face sloped lot conditions that affect foundation and drainage scope.

North Vancouver vs West Vancouver: Key Differences

While both municipalities are on the North Shore, the renovation conditions differ materially:

  • West Vancouver: Predominantly large lots, 1960s–1970s single-family homes, steep slope conditions in areas like Caulfeild and Cypress Park Estates. Most projects require a building permit and some require geotechnical review. The average assessed value of homes renovated in West Vancouver in 2025 was $2.4 million.
  • North Vancouver: Mix of 1950s–1980s homes, including many post-war bungalows and split-levels in areas like Boulevard, Blueridge, and Lynn Valley. More uniformity in lot size means more predictable structural conditions. Foundation work is more common due to sloped terrain in the Seymour neighbourhood.

What Permits Are Required for a Whole-House Renovation on the North Shore?

In both municipalities, a building permit is required whenever the scope includes structural changes, changes to exterior envelope, or work affecting footings and foundations. The following table summarizes permit requirements:

  • Interior-only cosmetic work: Building permit not required in most cases; electrical and plumbing permits may still apply
  • Kitchen or bathroom renovation with layout changes: Building permit required in both North Vancouver and West Vancouver
  • Structural modifications or new openings in load-bearing walls: Structural engineer letter required; building permit required
  • Additions or secondary suites: Building permit plus potentially a geotechnical report for sloped sites in both municipalities
  • Demolition of any portion of a post-and-beam structure: Requires structural engineering review and heritage consideration in West Vancouver

Reno Stars has managed building permit applications in both municipalities. Average permit processing time in North Vancouver is 4–6 weeks; in West Vancouver it is typically 6–10 weeks due to more rigorous review for hillside construction.

How Long Does a Whole House Renovation Take on the North Shore?

A whole-house renovation on the North Shore typically runs 4 to 10 months from permit application to final inspection, depending on scope and complexity:

  • Cosmetic renovation: 6–12 weeks
  • Standard full renovation: 4–6 months
  • Premium whole-house remodel with structural work: 6–10 months

West Vancouver projects average 3–4 weeks longer than North Vancouver equivalents due to more complex permit review and engineering requirements. Supply chain for specialty finishes — particularly custom glass railings and imported stone — should be factored into the schedule at the procurement stage, not after demolition.

What Is the Biggest Mistake North Shore Homeowners Make?

The most common error is underestimating what it costs to bring an older North Shore home up to current building code when opening walls. In West Vancouver, many homes built before 1980 contain asbestos in floor tiles and pipe insulation — a pre-demolition hazardous materials assessment is required before any scope begins, and removal must be performed by a licensed abatement contractor. In North Vancouver, the equivalent issue is knob-and-tube wiring in homes built before 1960, which must be fully replaced as part of any electrical upgrade.

Budgeting 10–15% contingency for unknowns behind closed walls is standard practice for North Shore renovations. Homes in West Vancouver's Ambleside and Dundarave neighbourhoods, in particular, frequently reveal unknown conditions once demolition begins.

Does the North Shore Have Specific Renovation Requirements for Secondary Suites?

Both North Vancouver and West Vancouver allow secondary suites in single-family zones, subject to size, parking, and fire separation requirements. In North Vancouver, the maximum suite size is 90 square metres (969 sq ft) for a one-bedroom or 110 square metres (1,184 sq ft) for a two-bedroom. In West Vancouver, suite regulations are more restrictive and vary by zone — always confirm with the District's building department before designing a suite. BC Housing provides provincial grant funding of up to $40,000 for approved secondary suite construction in both municipalities.

Frequently Asked Questions About Whole House Renovations on the North Shore

What does a whole-house renovation cost in North Vancouver in 2026?

A whole-house renovation in North Vancouver ranges from $180,000 for a standard remodel to $500,000 or more for a premium project with structural changes on a 2,000 square foot home. Cosmetic renovations start around $80,000. Actual cost depends on scope, condition of the existing structure, and whether engineering or hazardous materials remediation is required.

What does a whole-house renovation cost in West Vancouver in 2026?

West Vancouver renovations typically run higher than other Metro Vancouver municipalities due to larger average home size, older construction, and more complex permitting. A standard whole-house renovation in West Vancouver starts at approximately $220,000 and can reach $800,000 or more for premium remodels with structural engineering requirements.

Do I need a geotechnical report for a renovation in West Vancouver?

A geotechnical report is required for any renovation on a steep slope in West Vancouver, particularly in areas such as Caulfeild, Cypress Park Estates, and British Properties. Even minor foundation work on a sloped lot in these neighbourhoods typically requires a geotechnical engineer's sign-off as part of the building permit application.

How long does a whole-house renovation take in North Vancouver?

A whole-house renovation in North Vancouver takes 4 to 6 months on average for a standard remodel with permit. Cosmetic renovations run 6 to 12 weeks. Premium remodels with structural changes take 6 to 10 months. Permit processing adds 4–6 weeks at the front end.

Does West Vancouver allow secondary suites in renovated homes?

Yes, secondary suites are permitted in most single-family zones in West Vancouver, subject to size limits, parking requirements, and fire separation standards that vary by zone. Confirm suite eligibility with the District of West Vancouver building department before designing the layout. BC offers grants of up to $40,000 for approved secondary suite construction in West Vancouver.

北溫哥華和西溫哥華的獨立屋裝修並非單純的美化工程，而是涉及結構、地基和複雜行政程序的綜合項目。2026年，北溫和西溫的獨立屋全面裝修起價約為每平方呎180加元，視乎工程範圍，造價可達每平方呎500加元以上。

聚星裝修已完成北溫和西溫多個項目。本文根據大溫哥華58個真實項目數據，分析兩地實際造價、審批流程和工期差異。

北岸整屋裝修2026年造價是多少？

最終造價取決於三個因素：工程範圍、現有建築結構狀況，以及是否需要地震加固、坡地工程或文物保護審查。根據聚星裝修58個項目數據：

  • 表面翻新（地板、牆面油漆、櫥櫃翻新、浴室小修）：2,000平方呎住宅為80,000至180,000加元
  • 標準全面翻新（廚房和浴室重建、地板、水電重布、吊頂）：2,000平方呎住宅為180,000至380,000加元
  • 高端全面改造（結構改建、定制細木作、高端飾面、需工程師審查）：2,000平方呎住宅為380,000至800,000加元以上

西溫住宅平均偏向高端範圍。西溫大部分物業建於1960至1970年代，採用柱樑結構，任何改建前必須通過結構工程審查。北溫住宅則更常見坡地地形帶來的地基和排水工程需求。

北溫與西溫的核心差異

  • 西溫哥華：地塊大、獨立屋多為1960至1970年代建築，Caulfeild和Cypress Park Estates等地區坡度大。2025年西溫翻新住宅平均估值達240萬加元。
  • 北溫哥華：1950至1980年代住宅為主，包括Lynn Valley、Blueridge、Boulevard等區的戰後平房和錯層式住宅。地塊面積較一致，結構條件更可預測。Seymour小區坡地地形經常需要地基加固。

北岸裝修需要哪些許可證？

  • 僅室內表面工程：通常不需要建築許可證（但水電許可證仍可能需要）
  • 廚房或浴室改格局：北溫和西溫均需建築許可證
  • 結構改建或拆除承重牆：需結構工程師信函，建築許可證必備
  • 加建或後巷屋：需建築許可證，坡地可能需地質技術報告
  • 拆除柱樑結構任何部分（西溫）：需結構工程審查，可能涉及文物考慮

西溫平均審批時間比北溫長3至4週。

整屋翻新需要多長時間？

  • 表面翻新：6至12週
  • 標準全面翻新：4至6個月
  • 含結構改建的高端改造：6至10個月

北岸業主最常犯什麼錯誤？

最常見的錯誤是低估舊牆隱藏問題的處理成本。西溫1980年前住宅普遍存在石棉（地板瓷磚和管道保溫層），拆除前必須進行有害材料評估，由持證承包商進行處理。北溫1960年前住宅則常見knob-and-tube布線（紡織包覆電線），任何電翻新都必須全面更換。

北岸翻新建議預留10至15%應急預算，以應對開牆後可能發現的未知問題。西溫Ambleside和Dundarave小區尤為常見。

北岸允許翻新後加建後巷屋嗎？

北溫和西溫的獨立屋分區均允許後巷屋，但須符合面積、停車和防火隔離要求。北溫後巷屋最大面積為90平方米（一房）或110平方米（兩房）。西溫法規更嚴格且按分區而異，請在設計前向市政府確認。符合條件的後巷屋可獲BC省高達40,000加元補助。
